1	# Which declaration patterns does `--no-checker` miss? (census)
2	
3	Binary: origin/fix/bound-converted-type-size @ 50cd7dd0 (release, rust 1.99.1, CARGO_TARGET_DIR=shrink/target-census). `git fetch` failed (network denied in the sandbox), so that ref is the local copy and may be stale. Runs were `extract --src <src> --json --quiet --no-cache` with and without `--no-checker`, default `--collapse-inherited-props`, one process at a time under a 14 GB RSS watchdog (1 s sampling). Nothing was killed. Highest checker peak: Chakra 6456 MB; the others were under 900 MB. Short runs under 1 s show peak 0-2 MB, which is the sampling interval and not a real measurement. Outputs are in shrink/census/. Scripts: missing.py (per-component missing set), classify.js (TypeScript compiler API, syntax-only, same-file and relative-import resolution), extras.js (typeof import source, heritage text). Status: census/status.txt.
4	
5	"Missing" = a prop name the checker lists for a component (own + inherited member sets) and the structural answer does not. Components are matched by key; every component is in both answers (0 checker-only), so no component is lost, only props.
6	
7	## Summary
8	
9	- Antd and Mantine: 0 components with missing props. Chakra source corpus: 11 of 629 components, 13 props in total. The structural answer is complete enough there.
10	- Nearly all the loss is in two real corpora (shadcn 6228 props over 154 components, Spectrum 2216 over 34 components) and in the two synthetic Chakra consumer fixtures (chakra-only: 707 components, 507327 props; gate-large: 770 components, 508163 props; these overlap, do not add them).
11	- Style-prop sets (bucket counts of components by missing-prop count): chakra-only 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608, 1000+: 0. gate-large 111 / 51 / 608 / 0. shadcn 57 / 97 / 0 / 0. Spectrum 7 / 26 / 1 / 0. Chakra src 11 / 0 / 0 / 0. In the fixtures, 429163 of the missing props are parented to `SystemProperties` and 71500 to `Conditions`, both generated mapped/conditional types inside the installed `@chakra-ui/react` package. The structural answer lists 0 props for those components (e.g. `ChakraComboboxRoot`: 0 vs 899).
12	- All 706 fixture components declare props as `ComponentProps<typeof X>` where X is imported from the package `@chakra-ui/react` (706 of 706, checked from the import). Declared shape is simple; the content lives in node_modules.
13	- In shadcn, every missing prop has a node_modules parent (`GlobalDOMEvents` 6171, `HTMLAttributes` 57). Each affected component loses the same roughly 60-63 DOM event handlers (onAnimationEnd, onMouseDown, onPointerMove, ...). Declared shapes are all simple (intersection, Omit, ComponentProps, direct named type); the props come from `react-aria-components`, `cmdk`, `radix-ui` types.
14	- In Spectrum, 32 of 34 components are wrapped in `createLeafComponent` / `createBranchComponent`, and their props interfaces extend several in-repo interfaces (`Omit<GlobalDOMAttributes<..>,'onClick'>`, `LinkDOMProps`, `PressEvents`, `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>`). The checker lists ~100 props, the structural answer 1 (ListBoxItem 102 vs 1).
15	- The Chakra source corpus misses only `ref` and recipe variant keys (`inline`, `placement`) on `chakra("div", {...variants})` components.
16	
17	## Buckets (real corpora = shadcn + Spectrum + Chakra src; 199 components, 8457 missing props)
18	
19	Primary bucket is the shape of the top-level declared props type (same-file and relative-import resolved), first in the order you listed; the factory/generic/polymorphic/recipe tags only win when the top shape is unresolvable. Overlap counts (components carrying a tag anywhere): shadcn external 70, componentprops 78, wrapper 33, intersection 54, generic 19, unresolved 12; Spectrum factory 32, generic 24, extends 24, componentprops 23, wrapper 17, recipe 10. Fixtures: componentprops 706 of 707. No component had a top-level mapped, conditional, or indexed shape. Polymorphic `as` tagged none that matter. Nothing used `SystemStyleObject` spreads in these components.
20	
21	- Intersection of named types: 54 components (all shadcn), 2932 props, 34.7%. Examples: AlertDialog (`Omit<ModalOverlayPrimitiveProps,"className"|"children"> & Pick<ComponentProps<typeof ModalPrimitive>,"isDismissable"> & {...}`), missing onAnimationEnd, onAnimationEndCapture, onAnimationIteration, onAnimationIterationCapture, onAnimationStart...; BreadcrumbItem (`BreadcrumbProps & {separatorClassName?}`); TraceCollapsibleTrigger (`Omit<ButtonProps,"className"|"children"|"slot"> & {...}`).
22	- Interface extends other interfaces: 24 components (all Spectrum), 1874 props, 22.2%. Examples: ListBoxItem (101 missing: onBlur, onFocus, onFocusChange, dir, hidden, inert, lang, suppressHydrationWarning), MenuItem (100), Row (99: render, dir, hidden, inert...).
23	- `ComponentProps<typeof X>` family: 51 shadcn components, 1427 props, 16.9% (real corpora); plus 706 fixture components, 506621 props. Examples: AlertDialogContent (`React.ComponentProps<typeof AlertDialog>`, 64), ButtonGroupSeparator (`ComponentProps<typeof Separator>`, 64), Textarea (1: `tw`); fixtures ChakraComboboxRoot (899: recipe, allowCustomValue, alwaysSubmitOnEnter, autoFocus...), ChakraSelectRoot (887: recipe, id, 2xl, 2xlDown...).
24	- Other, a named props type imported from a package (23 `react-aria-components`, 8 unresolved namespace imports such as `ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`): 31 shadcn components plus 2 Spectrum, 1050 props, 12.4%. Examples: Accordion (`DisclosureGroupProps`, 64), AccordionContent (`DisclosurePanelProps`, 64), TableHead (`ColumnProps`, 64); Spectrum `_Card` (12: childItems, hasChildItems, textValue, title; initializer is an `as` expression) and Column (3, declaration not found by name).
25	- Generic (named external generic, `ListBoxProps<T>`): 15 shadcn components, 831 props, 9.8%. Examples: BreadcrumbList (`BreadcrumbsProps<T>`, 64), ComboboxGroup (`ListBoxSectionProps<T>`, 64), TableRow (`RowProps<T>`, 63).
26	- Factory/callee call: 11 Chakra + 4 Spectrum components, 335 props, 4.0%. Examples: Chakra Center (`chakra("div",{base,variants})`: inline, ref), InputElement (placement, ref); Spectrum MenuSection (`createBranchComponent`, 85: render, dir, hidden, inert), Divider (81: aria-describedby, aria-details, aria-label, aria-labelledby).
27	- Plain literal / interface without heritage: 4 Spectrum components, 5 props (Divider `{size?}`, SubmenuTrigger children/delay): the factory wrapper hides them from the structural reader.
28	- Wrapper (Omit/Pick/Partial) as top shape: 3 shadcn components, 3 props (AlertDialogTitle, DialogTitle, SheetTitle: `tw`).
29	- Mapped, conditional, indexed, recipe, polymorphic as top shape: 0 components.
30	
31	## Rule-coverability judgement (candid; I did not implement any rule)
32	
33	- Intersection and Omit/Pick wrapper (shadcn): the declared shape is trivial to parse. A rule would resolve each member, apply Omit/Pick as a key filter and union the members. The blocker is that the member types live in `react-aria-components` d.ts, so a rule needs package/d.ts resolution. Uncovered by inspection: whether those d.ts use only plain interface heritage (then a deterministic walker is enough) or `GlobalDOMAttributes<T>`-style generics over `@types/react`. I only know the parent names, not their definitions. About 100% of these missing props have a node_modules parent. Risk: Omit keys given as unions/aliases, class names mismatched.
34	- Interface extends (Spectrum): a rule would walk heritage across workspace packages (`@react-types/shared`, `react-aria`) and flatten, applying `Omit<X,'k'>` as a filter. Two of its inputs are not plain: `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>` looks conditional on the tag, and `GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` is generic. Plain heritage (`LinkDOMProps`, `HoverEvents`, `PressEvents`) is rule-coverable given workspace resolution. The structural side listed 1 prop of 102 for ListBoxItem, so heritage across modules is currently not flattened. Likely partial coverage: most of the 100 props come from the plain interfaces and the DOM event set; the conditional alias is the uncertain part.
35	- `ComponentProps<typeof X>`: if X is local or a workspace/aliased file (shadcn: 9 local, 20 `@/registry/...` aliases), rule = resolve X to its function, take its first param type, recurse. That needs tsconfig `paths`. If X comes from node_modules (`react-aria-components` 28, `cmdk` 21, `radix-ui`, `react-day-picker`; fixtures: `@chakra-ui/react` 706 of 706) the rule needs the d.ts, and for Chakra the 429163 `SystemProperties` + 71500 `Conditions` props come from generated mapped/conditional types. That bucket needs type evaluation unless the owner accepts a fixed lookup table of Chakra's style-prop names (about 845 names per recipe) keyed on the package version. Fragile, and I have no evidence the set is stable across components.
36	- Other / generic named type from a package: same as above; plus type-argument substitution for `X<T>` (generic default `T = object` is likely irrelevant to prop names, a cheap assumption I did not verify). Namespace imports (`ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`) need namespace resolution.
37	- Factory (Chakra): `chakra("div", {variants})` is rule-coverable from the call arguments. The 13 missing props are `ref` (added by the factory) and variant keys (`inline`, `placement`), but evidence is 3 components, so the rule is only supported on small samples. Spectrum `createLeafComponent('x', function(props: P, ref, item){})`: coverable by reading the first function parameter, then it falls into the extends bucket. Two Spectrum initializers (as-expression, a nested call) were not unwrapped by my classifier either.
38	- Highest-value order by missing props: intersection (2932), extends (1874), ComponentProps (1427 + 506621 in the fixtures), other (1050), generic (831). None of the five is rule-coverable without module/package resolution; only the factory bucket (4%) is covered by the call arguments alone. Within real corpora, roughly the Spectrum 22% and the local-alias part of ComponentProps are coverable with workspace resolution; the node_modules-parented shadcn losses (and the Chakra fixtures) need the checker or a bundled type-declaration reader.
39	
40	## Caveats
41	
42	- Classification is syntax-only plus resolution through same-file declarations and relative imports; path aliases (`@/...`) and workspace packages are not resolved, which is why several shapes read "external". Top-shape bucket uses that resolution; tags are best-effort.
43	- Default `--collapse-inherited-props` was used (as asked), not `none`.
44	- The reverse direction (struct-only props; e.g. Chakra struct lists 1118 props vs checker 845 on Center) was not analysed.
45	- Missing-prop names for a few examples are limited to the first 5-8 listed above.
46	- A first accidental build ran with the default toolchain into the worktree `target/` dir (ignored by git) before the proper one; that dir is unused.
47	
48	## Appendix: per-corpus counts
49	
50	- chakra-ui (packages/react/src): 629 checker components, 629 structural, 11 with missing props, 13 missing props. Buckets 1-10: 11. All `factory` (chakra("tag",...)).
51	- mantine: 348 / 348, 0 missing.
52	- ant-design (components): 254 / 254, 0 missing.
53	- react-spectrum (packages): 1415 / 1415, 34 with missing, 2216 props. Buckets 1-10: 7, 11-100: 26, 101-1000: 1. Extends 24 (1874), factory 4 (322), plain 4 (5), other 2 (15).
54	- shadcn-ui (apps/v4): 1901 / 1901, 154 with missing, 6228 props. Buckets 1-10: 57, 11-100: 97. Intersection 54 (2932), componentprops 51 (1427), other 31 (1035), generic 15 (831), wrapper 3 (3).
55	- checker-default/chakra-only: 788 / 788, 707 with missing, 507327 props. Buckets 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 706 (506621), intersection 1 (706).
56	- gate-large: 938 / 938, 770 with missing, 508163 props. Buckets 1-10: 111, 11-100: 51, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 769 (507457), intersection 1 (706).
57	- Runs: all exit 0. Peak RSS: chakra checker 6456 MB, gate-large 871, antd 886, shadcn 856, spectrum 732, others under 1 GB or unsampled.
58

Runs were `extract --src <src> --json --quiet --no-cache` with and without `--no-checker`, default `--collapse-inherited-props`, one process at a time under a 14 GB RSS watchdog (1 s sampling). Nothing was killed. Highest checker peak: Chakra 6456 MB; the others were under 900 MB. Short runs under 1 s show peak 0-2 MB, which is the sampling interval and not a real measurement. Outputs are in shrink/census/. Scripts: missing.py (per-component missing set), classify.js (TypeScript compiler API, syntax-only, same-file and relative-import resolution), extras.js (typeof import source, heritage text). Status: census/status.txt.

"Missing" = a prop name the checker lists for a component (own + inherited member sets) and the structural answer does not. Components are matched by key; every component is in both answers (0 checker-only), so no component is lost, only props.

## Summary

- Antd and Mantine: 0 components with missing props. Chakra source corpus: 11 of 629 components, 13 props in total. The structural answer is complete enough there.
- Nearly all the loss is in two real corpora (shadcn 6228 props over 154 components, Spectrum 2216 over 34 components) and in the two synthetic Chakra consumer fixtures (chakra-only: 707 components, 507327 props; gate-large: 770 components, 508163 props; these overlap, do not add them).
- Style-prop sets (bucket counts of components by missing-prop count): chakra-only 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608, 1000+: 0. gate-large 111 / 51 / 608 / 0. shadcn 57 / 97 / 0 / 0. Spectrum 7 / 26 / 1 / 0. Chakra src 11 / 0 / 0 / 0. In the fixtures, 429163 of the missing props are parented to `SystemProperties` and 71500 to `Conditions`, both generated mapped/conditional types inside the installed `@chakra-ui/react` package. The structural answer lists 0 props for those components (e.g. `ChakraComboboxRoot`: 0 vs 899).
- All 706 fixture components declare props as `ComponentProps<typeof X>` where X is imported from the package `@chakra-ui/react` (706 of 706, checked from the import). Declared shape is simple; the content lives in node_modules.
- In shadcn, every missing prop has a node_modules parent (`GlobalDOMEvents` 6171, `HTMLAttributes` 57). Each affected component loses the same roughly 60-63 DOM event handlers (onAnimationEnd, onMouseDown, onPointerMove, ...). Declared shapes are all simple (intersection, Omit, ComponentProps, direct named type); the props come from `react-aria-components`, `cmdk`, `radix-ui` types.
- In Spectrum, 32 of 34 components are wrapped in `createLeafComponent` / `createBranchComponent`, and their props interfaces extend several in-repo interfaces (`Omit<GlobalDOMAttributes<..>,'onClick'>`, `LinkDOMProps`, `PressEvents`, `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>`). The checker lists ~100 props, the structural answer 1 (ListBoxItem 102 vs 1).
- The Chakra source corpus misses only `ref` and recipe variant keys (`inline`, `placement`) on `chakra("div", {...variants})` components.

## Buckets (real corpora = shadcn + Spectrum + Chakra src; 199 components, 8457 missing props)

Primary bucket is the shape of the top-level declared props type (same-file and relative-import resolved), first in the order you listed; the factory/generic/polymorphic/recipe tags only win when the top shape is unresolvable. Overlap counts (components carrying a tag anywhere): shadcn external 70, componentprops 78, wrapper 33, intersection 54, generic 19, unresolved 12; Spectrum factory 32, generic 24, extends 24, componentprops 23, wrapper 17, recipe 10. Fixtures: componentprops 706 of 707. No component had a top-level mapped, conditional, or indexed shape. Polymorphic `as` tagged none that matter. Nothing used `SystemStyleObject` spreads in these components.

- Intersection of named types: 54 components (all shadcn), 2932 props, 34.7%. Examples: AlertDialog (`Omit<ModalOverlayPrimitiveProps,"className"|"children"> & Pick<ComponentProps<typeof ModalPrimitive>,"isDismissable"> & {...}`), missing onAnimationEnd, onAnimationEndCapture, onAnimationIteration, onAnimationIterationCapture, onAnimationStart...; BreadcrumbItem (`BreadcrumbProps & {separatorClassName?}`); TraceCollapsibleTrigger (`Omit<ButtonProps,"className"|"children"|"slot"> & {...}`).
- Interface extends other interfaces: 24 components (all Spectrum), 1874 props, 22.2%. Examples: ListBoxItem (101 missing: onBlur, onFocus, onFocusChange, dir, hidden, inert, lang, suppressHydrationWarning), MenuItem (100), Row (99: render, dir, hidden, inert...).
- `ComponentProps<typeof X>` family: 51 shadcn components, 1427 props, 16.9% (real corpora); plus 706 fixture components, 506621 props. Examples: AlertDialogContent (`React.ComponentProps<typeof AlertDialog>`, 64), ButtonGroupSeparator (`ComponentProps<typeof Separator>`, 64), Textarea (1: `tw`); fixtures ChakraComboboxRoot (899: recipe, allowCustomValue, alwaysSubmitOnEnter, autoFocus...), ChakraSelectRoot (887: recipe, id, 2xl, 2xlDown...).
- Other, a named props type imported from a package (23 `react-aria-components`, 8 unresolved namespace imports such as `ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`): 31 shadcn components plus 2 Spectrum, 1050 props, 12.4%. Examples: Accordion (`DisclosureGroupProps`, 64), AccordionContent (`DisclosurePanelProps`, 64), TableHead (`ColumnProps`, 64); Spectrum `_Card` (12: childItems, hasChildItems, textValue, title; initializer is an `as` expression) and Column (3, declaration not found by name).
- Generic (named external generic, `ListBoxProps<T>`): 15 shadcn components, 831 props, 9.8%. Examples: BreadcrumbList (`BreadcrumbsProps<T>`, 64), ComboboxGroup (`ListBoxSectionProps<T>`, 64), TableRow (`RowProps<T>`, 63).
- Factory/callee call: 11 Chakra + 4 Spectrum components, 335 props, 4.0%. Examples: Chakra Center (`chakra("div",{base,variants})`: inline, ref), InputElement (placement, ref); Spectrum MenuSection (`createBranchComponent`, 85: render, dir, hidden, inert), Divider (81: aria-describedby, aria-details, aria-label, aria-labelledby).
- Plain literal / interface without heritage: 4 Spectrum components, 5 props (Divider `{size?}`, SubmenuTrigger children/delay): the factory wrapper hides them from the structural reader.
- Wrapper (Omit/Pick/Partial) as top shape: 3 shadcn components, 3 props (AlertDialogTitle, DialogTitle, SheetTitle: `tw`).
- Mapped, conditional, indexed, recipe, polymorphic as top shape: 0 components.

## Rule-coverability judgement (candid; I did not implement any rule)

- Intersection and Omit/Pick wrapper (shadcn): the declared shape is trivial to parse. A rule would resolve each member, apply Omit/Pick as a key filter and union the members. The blocker is that the member types live in `react-aria-components` d.ts, so a rule needs package/d.ts resolution. Uncovered by inspection: whether those d.ts use only plain interface heritage (then a deterministic walker is enough) or `GlobalDOMAttributes<T>`-style generics over `@types/react`. I only know the parent names, not their definitions. About 100% of these missing props have a node_modules parent. Risk: Omit keys given as unions/aliases, class names mismatched.
- Interface extends (Spectrum): a rule would walk heritage across workspace packages (`@react-types/shared`, `react-aria`) and flatten, applying `Omit<X,'k'>` as a filter. Two of its inputs are not plain: `PossibleLinkDOMRenderProps<'div', R>` looks conditional on the tag, and `GlobalDOMAttributes<HTMLDivElement>` is generic. Plain heritage (`LinkDOMProps`, `HoverEvents`, `PressEvents`) is rule-coverable given workspace resolution. The structural side listed 1 prop of 102 for ListBoxItem, so heritage across modules is currently not flattened. Likely partial coverage: most of the 100 props come from the plain interfaces and the DOM event set; the conditional alias is the uncertain part.
- `ComponentProps<typeof X>`: if X is local or a workspace/aliased file (shadcn: 9 local, 20 `@/registry/...` aliases), rule = resolve X to its function, take its first param type, recurse. That needs tsconfig `paths`. If X comes from node_modules (`react-aria-components` 28, `cmdk` 21, `radix-ui`, `react-day-picker`; fixtures: `@chakra-ui/react` 706 of 706) the rule needs the d.ts, and for Chakra the 429163 `SystemProperties` + 71500 `Conditions` props come from generated mapped/conditional types. That bucket needs type evaluation unless the owner accepts a fixed lookup table of Chakra's style-prop names (about 845 names per recipe) keyed on the package version. Fragile, and I have no evidence the set is stable across components.
- Other / generic named type from a package: same as above; plus type-argument substitution for `X<T>` (generic default `T = object` is likely irrelevant to prop names, a cheap assumption I did not verify). Namespace imports (`ResizablePrimitive.PanelProps`) need namespace resolution.
- Factory (Chakra): `chakra("div", {variants})` is rule-coverable from the call arguments. The 13 missing props are `ref` (added by the factory) and variant keys (`inline`, `placement`), but evidence is 3 components, so the rule is only supported on small samples. Spectrum `createLeafComponent('x', function(props: P, ref, item){})`: coverable by reading the first function parameter, then it falls into the extends bucket. Two Spectrum initializers (as-expression, a nested call) were not unwrapped by my classifier either.
- Highest-value order by missing props: intersection (2932), extends (1874), ComponentProps (1427 + 506621 in the fixtures), other (1050), generic (831). None of the five is rule-coverable without module/package resolution; only the factory bucket (4%) is covered by the call arguments alone. Within real corpora, roughly the Spectrum 22% and the local-alias part of ComponentProps are coverable with workspace resolution; the node_modules-parented shadcn losses (and the Chakra fixtures) need the checker or a bundled type-declaration reader.

## Caveats

- Classification is syntax-only plus resolution through same-file declarations and relative imports; path aliases (`@/...`) and workspace packages are not resolved, which is why several shapes read "external". Top-shape bucket uses that resolution; tags are best-effort.
- Default `--collapse-inherited-props` was used (as asked), not `none`.
- The reverse direction (struct-only props; e.g. Chakra struct lists 1118 props vs checker 845 on Center) was not analysed.
- Missing-prop names for a few examples are limited to the first 5-8 listed above.
- A first accidental build ran with the default toolchain into the worktree `target/` dir (ignored by git) before the proper one; that dir is unused.

## Appendix: per-corpus counts

- chakra-ui (packages/react/src): 629 checker components, 629 structural, 11 with missing props, 13 missing props. Buckets 1-10: 11. All `factory` (chakra("tag",...)).
- mantine: 348 / 348, 0 missing.
- ant-design (components): 254 / 254, 0 missing.
- react-spectrum (packages): 1415 / 1415, 34 with missing, 2216 props. Buckets 1-10: 7, 11-100: 26, 101-1000: 1. Extends 24 (1874), factory 4 (322), plain 4 (5), other 2 (15).
- shadcn-ui (apps/v4): 1901 / 1901, 154 with missing, 6228 props. Buckets 1-10: 57, 11-100: 97. Intersection 54 (2932), componentprops 51 (1427), other 31 (1035), generic 15 (831), wrapper 3 (3).
- checker-default/chakra-only: 788 / 788, 707 with missing, 507327 props. Buckets 1-10: 82, 11-100: 17, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 706 (506621), intersection 1 (706).
- gate-large: 938 / 938, 770 with missing, 508163 props. Buckets 1-10: 111, 11-100: 51, 101-1000: 608. ComponentProps 769 (507457), intersection 1 (706).
- Runs: all exit 0. Peak RSS: chakra checker 6456 MB, gate-large 871, antd 886, shadcn 856, spectrum 732, others under 1 GB or unsampled.

1	# Chakra whole-project extract: 42 GB with the checker on
2	
3	Date: 2026-11-15. Binary: release-candidate-target/release/caliper-docgen (0.11.0, main 7b8f6d0d). Corpus: corpora/chakra-ui/packages/react/src.
4	
5	## Summary
6	
7	- The 42 GB is the Rust heap of the converter's output types (`PropType` trees), not the tsrs checker arenas. mimalloc stats at exit: peak commit 43.5 GiB in mimalloc's own arenas (tsrs arenas are a separate `mmap` range, `tsrs_core-0.24.0/src/reserve.rs:86`), with peak RSS 40.4 GiB, so almost all of it is mimalloc-allocated Rust memory.
8	- Why it is so large: in this corpus Chakra's style system (`styled-system/`) is *project source*, so `is_own` (crates/semantic/src/convert.rs:339) treats its ~700 `SystemProperties` and its 130 `Conditions` as the project's own members, and `MAX_FIELDS` never cuts own members (convert.rs:1249, "What the project declared itself is never cut"). Every `_hover`, `sm`, `css`, ... prop (type `SystemStyleObject`) expands to about 700 fields × (value union + a 130-field condition object): 24.7 MB of JSON *each*. In the gate fixture (`checker-default/chakra-only`) the same types come from `node_modules`, are a dependency's, and stop at a named boundary, so the gates never saw this.
9	- The multiplier: `Converter::convert` returns `entry.converted.clone()` on every memo hit (convert.rs:681-686), a deep clone of the tree, and `PropType` has no shared children. The run made 1,729,385 memo hits against 74,401 misses (`type_memo=(1729385, 74401)` in the `-vv` log). Output is 3.87 GB of JSON, and memory is about 10 times that.
10	- Why the guard missed it: the arena guard (`max_rss_mib`, 768 MiB, `Upkeep::decide`) exists only in `OnDemand` (crates/semantic/src/on_demand.rs:491, 646, 656), which serves the Storybook/watch session. `extract` calls the one-shot `resolve_cached_early`/`resolve_early`/`resolve` (crates/cli/src/commands/extract.rs:187-190, crates/semantic/src/lib.rs:159-208), which has no memory check. Even if it were wired in, it reads only the tsrs arena range with `mincore` (crates/semantic/src/checker.rs:164-171), which leaves out the converter heap where the 40 GB lives. It also checks only between requests, and the first parallel batch of 5 components alone built 39 GB in 5 s.
11	- Recommended bound (two parts):
12	  - A size cut in the converter: a converted type larger than a byte or node budget becomes a named `Truncated`. Prototyped with a 256 KB budget: Chakra goes from 41.8 GB / 14.8 s / 3.87 GB output to 4.36 GB / 4.8 s / 108 MB, and the output is byte-identical (stats excluded) on Mantine core and on the gate fixture.
13	  - A hard heap budget on the one-shot path as the safety net: past it, the remaining components keep their structural answer, with one warning diagnostic.
14	  - Sharing memo results (no deep clone) is the follow-up that removes the remaining ~40× ratio of memory to output.
15	
16	## 1. Reproduction and where the memory lives
17	
18	- Default (checker on, fresh `--cache-dir`): exit 0, 14.84 s real, 29.9 s user, max RSS 43,413,766,144 B, peak footprint 41,844,472,552 B (39.0 GiB).
19	- mimalloc (`MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1`): arenas reserved peak 44.3 GiB, committed peak 43.5 GiB, purged 40.8 GiB, peak rss 40.4 GiB, 45 threads peak.
20	- RSS samples (0.3 s apart, MiB): 171, 583, 785, 1041, 4741, 11330, 17862, 23984, 30197, 34850, 35902, 37681, 39231, 39905, then flat at about 40 GB for about 7 s, a bump to 41.3 GB at the end (kept-answer save and JSON write), then a slow decline. The climb is the first 4 s of checker work.
21	- `--no-cache -vv` (no kept answer): footprint 41,847,880,472 B, the same. So the kept answer is not the cause. Phase log:
22	  - Program built in 61 ms.
23	  - The first 5 components (`ArrowDownIcon`, `AspectRatio`, `AccordionItem`, `ActionBarCloseTrigger`, `Badge`) each took about 5,080 ms and about 7,100 checker requests. RSS went from 1 GB to 39 GB over exactly those 5 s.
24	  - Every later component took 2 to 650 ms, served from the memo.
25	  - The backend finished at total_ms=7366 with `type_memo=(1729385, 74401)`.
26	- Ruled out:
27	  - tsrs arenas: they are a separate mmap range, and mimalloc's commit alone accounts for the RSS.
28	  - JSON writer: it streams through a 64 KiB `BufWriter` (extract.rs:82), and the RSS plateau comes before writing.
29	  - Kept answer: `--no-cache` peaks the same. It does add a transient copy, because `kept::save` builds the whole 2.16 GB msgpack in one `Vec` before writing (crates/semantic/src/kept.rs:332-339), so `checker-answers.msgpack` is 2,155 MB on disk.
30	- `--no-checker`: 0.2 s, 385 MiB (the caller's number, not re-run).
31	
32	## 2. Counts and what in Chakra makes it this size
33	
34	- Components: 629 extracted, 620 resolved by the checker, 9 kept structural (not exported), 3 props degraded.
35	- Interned prop entries in the output `props` table: 3,708. Prop references in the components' `props` arrays: 4,432 (at most 16 per component; the style props sit in the props table and inherited layers).
36	- Output JSON: 3,870,036,382 bytes. Component section: 514 KB. Props table: 3.869 GB. Diagnostics: about 0.3 MB.
37	- Size distribution of props: median 759 B, p90 152 KB, p99 24.7 MB. 151 props over 1 MB hold 3.72 GB (96%); 574 more are between 100 KB and 1 MB.
38	  - About 125 condition and breakpoint props (`_hover`, `_focus`, `_peerChecked`, `sm`, `mdToXl`, `2xlOnly`, `base`, `css`, `styles`, ...) of type `SystemStyleObject` = `Nested<SystemProperties & CssVarProperties>` (styled-system/css.types.ts:57): 24.68 MB each.
39	  - 8 slot props (`rootProps`, `startAddonProps`, `endAddonProps`, `startElementProps`, `endElementProps`, `branchProps`, `branchContentProps`, `children`) of about 45.5 MB each, which embed the style props.
40	  - `rowStart`/`colSpan`/... 9 MB, `placement` 17 MB, `direction` 12 MB.
41	- Source shapes:
42	  - styled-system/generated/system.gen.ts: 793 lines, 706 optional properties.
43	  - conditions.gen.ts: `Conditions` with 130 keys.
44	  - Each style property is `ConditionalValue<V>` (css.types.ts:32), which includes a `{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: ... }` object of 130 fields, each a depth-truncated text.
45	  - So one `SystemStyleObject` is about 706 × (literal union + 130 fields), and each of about 125 props holds its own copy.
46	- `--collapse-inherited-props none` (the weekly) does not change this. With the 256 KB prototype the weekly flags gave the same 108 MB output and 4.33 GB as the default. The weekly's extra cost on 0.11.0 (31.8 s, 42.7 GB) is the same blow-up.
47	- In the gate fixture (chakra-only, 787 components), the largest prop is 26 KB: there `@chakra-ui/react`'s style system is a dependency, so `SystemStyleObject` stays a name.
48	
49	## 3. Why the arena guard did not bound it
50	
51	- The bound exists only in `OnDemand`:
52	  - `DEFAULT_MAX_RSS_MIB = 768` (on_demand.rs:71).
53	  - It is checked in `warm` (on_demand.rs:491) and in `maintain` after each served request (on_demand.rs:643-652, gated by `Upkeep::checks_memory(self.served)`).
54	  - `stop_past_bound` (on_demand.rs:655-669) turns the checker off for the session.
55	  - `OnDemand` is used by the Storybook provider, the watch path and the binding, not by `extract`.
56	- `extract` takes `Pass::Extract` and uses `Teardown::OneShot` (extract.rs:181), then calls `resolve_cached_early`, `resolve_early` or `resolve` (extract.rs:187-190, lib.rs:159-208). None of them reads memory or carries a `max_rss_mib`.
57	- What the guard measures: `arena_mib()` runs `mincore` over `tsrs_core::reserve::base()..RESERVE` (checker.rs:164-171). That is the checker's nodes, symbols and types only. The converter's `PropType` trees, the memo (`State::memo`, convert.rs:495), `KeptProps`, `PartsSeen` and the merged `ParsedProp`s are all mimalloc heap, outside that range. A 768 MiB arena bound would read a few hundred MiB here while the process held 40 GB.
58	- When it checks: between requests. The 39 GB is built inside the first concurrent batch of 5 components (about 5 s), so a per-request check is too late even in `OnDemand`. A Storybook session opening one of those 5 components would build the same multi-GB tree before any check.
59	- The ADR 0026 memory gate measured `chakra-only` (dependency style system, 785 MiB) and the arena, so neither the fixture nor the metric could see a project-source style system.
60	
61	## 4. Proposed bound
62	
63	Part A: the size cut in the converter (keeps semantic answers, bounds output).
64	- Rule: in `Converter::convert` (convert.rs:674-700), after `uncached`, a converted type whose size passes a budget is replaced by `Truncated` with its name (`self.truncated`, convert.rs:953), and the memo stores the cut form. Measure the size as a node count kept alongside the memo entry, rather than serializing as the prototype does.
65	- Prototype (uncommitted, reverted in worktree agent-ae859a360675978f3): `serde_json::to_vec(&converted).len() > PROTO_MAX_BYTES` → `self.truncated(info, None, TruncationLimit::Depth)`.
66	  - 1,000,000 B budget: Chakra 6.47 GB footprint, 5.08 s, 178 MB output.
67	  - 256,000 B budget: Chakra 4.36 GB, 4.81 s, 108 MB output. With weekly flags: 4.33 GB, 4.73 s.
68	  - Mantine core (`packages/@mantine/core/src`; largest prop 196 KB): output identical with both budgets (stats excluded); 0.87 GB both ways.
69	  - Gate fixture `checker-default/chakra-only/src`: identical, about 0.70 GB.
70	- Rejected variant: capping project-declared objects below the top at 100 fields gets Chakra to 1.16 GB, 2.3 s and 10.7 MB, but changes Mantine's output (`classNames`, `styles`, `vars`, `getInputProps` in 24 of 348 components). It is not output-preserving.
71	- Budget choice: Mantine's largest whole prop is 196 KB, so 256 KB is close to it. 512 KB to 1 MB gives more margin at 4.4 to 6.5 GB. A node-count budget should be calibrated on the four weekly corpora before choosing.
72	- Needs a new `TruncationLimit` variant (for example `Size { nodes }`) or a documented reuse, plus a diagnostic. That is a schema and contract decision (ADR).
73	
74	Part B: the hard heap budget on the one-shot path (guarantees a bound for any shape).
75	- Count converted nodes or bytes in a shared `AtomicU64` in `State`, incremented on each miss and each memo-hit clone (the size is known from the entry). Alternatively read mimalloc's committed bytes (`mi_process_info`), which also sees the clone.
76	- When the count passes `max_heap_mib` (default about 4 GiB, configurable, with the same knob reused by `OnDemand`), `convert` returns a new `CallError` variant. The component in flight, and every later one, keeps its structural answer. One `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning names the bound, as `stop_past_bound` does.
77	- Checked inside the conversion, not between requests, so the first batch cannot run away.
78	- Output under the bound is unchanged by construction. Gate fixture and Mantine are under 1 GB.
79	
80	Part C (follow-up, not needed for the bound): stop deep-cloning on memo hits. Share converted subtrees (`Arc<PropType>` children, or a type table with references) so that a hit costs one pointer. This attacks the remaining ~40× ratio of memory to output (108 MB output → 4.36 GB). It touches the public core type and the serializers, so it is a larger change.
81	
82	Also worth doing: `kept::save` should stream to the temporary file (`rmp_serde::encode::write` into a `BufWriter`) instead of building the whole buffer, which was 2.16 GB here.
83	
84	Risks:
85	- The size cut changes output only for types over the budget. A project with legitimately large own types (a design-token object) loses their expansion, and a diagnostic must say so.
86	- Measuring size after `uncached` still builds the oversized tree once, transiently, per in-flight conversion (tens to hundreds of MB × up to 4 converters). Part B covers the worst case.
87	- The memo stores the cut form, so a type cut at one depth stays cut wherever it is recalled at that depth, as the existing caps already do.
88	- Part B makes results depend on a memory threshold. Past it, which components stay structural depends on order. The answer order is deterministic, but the result differs between machines if the default is derived from RAM, so keep it a constant.
89	- Serializing to measure (prototype) costs time: 1.0 → 1.35 s on Mantine. Use a node count.
90	- Add a gate fixture with a project-source style system (the Chakra corpus `src` itself, or a trimmed copy) to the ADR 0026 memory gate, measured as process footprint rather than arena residency.
91

- Default (checker on, fresh `--cache-dir`): exit 0, 14.84 s real, 29.9 s user, max RSS 43,413,766,144 B, peak footprint 41,844,472,552 B (39.0 GiB).
- mimalloc (`MIMALLOC_SHOW_STATS=1`): arenas reserved peak 44.3 GiB, committed peak 43.5 GiB, purged 40.8 GiB, peak rss 40.4 GiB, 45 threads peak.
- RSS samples (0.3 s apart, MiB): 171, 583, 785, 1041, 4741, 11330, 17862, 23984, 30197, 34850, 35902, 37681, 39231, 39905, then flat at about 40 GB for about 7 s, a bump to 41.3 GB at the end (kept-answer save and JSON write), then a slow decline. The climb is the first 4 s of checker work.
- `--no-cache -vv` (no kept answer): footprint 41,847,880,472 B, the same. So the kept answer is not the cause. Phase log:
  - Program built in 61 ms.
  - The first 5 components (`ArrowDownIcon`, `AspectRatio`, `AccordionItem`, `ActionBarCloseTrigger`, `Badge`) each took about 5,080 ms and about 7,100 checker requests. RSS went from 1 GB to 39 GB over exactly those 5 s.
  - Every later component took 2 to 650 ms, served from the memo.
  - The backend finished at total_ms=7366 with `type_memo=(1729385, 74401)`.
- Ruled out:
  - tsrs arenas: they are a separate mmap range, and mimalloc's commit alone accounts for the RSS.
  - JSON writer: it streams through a 64 KiB `BufWriter` (extract.rs:82), and the RSS plateau comes before writing.
  - Kept answer: `--no-cache` peaks the same. It does add a transient copy, because `kept::save` builds the whole 2.16 GB msgpack in one `Vec` before writing (crates/semantic/src/kept.rs:332-339), so `checker-answers.msgpack` is 2,155 MB on disk.
- `--no-checker`: 0.2 s, 385 MiB (the caller's number, not re-run).

## 2. Counts and what in Chakra makes it this size

- Components: 629 extracted, 620 resolved by the checker, 9 kept structural (not exported), 3 props degraded.
- Interned prop entries in the output `props` table: 3,708. Prop references in the components' `props` arrays: 4,432 (at most 16 per component; the style props sit in the props table and inherited layers).
- Output JSON: 3,870,036,382 bytes. Component section: 514 KB. Props table: 3.869 GB. Diagnostics: about 0.3 MB.
- Size distribution of props: median 759 B, p90 152 KB, p99 24.7 MB. 151 props over 1 MB hold 3.72 GB (96%); 574 more are between 100 KB and 1 MB.
  - About 125 condition and breakpoint props (`_hover`, `_focus`, `_peerChecked`, `sm`, `mdToXl`, `2xlOnly`, `base`, `css`, `styles`, ...) of type `SystemStyleObject` = `Nested<SystemProperties & CssVarProperties>` (styled-system/css.types.ts:57): 24.68 MB each.
  - 8 slot props (`rootProps`, `startAddonProps`, `endAddonProps`, `startElementProps`, `endElementProps`, `branchProps`, `branchContentProps`, `children`) of about 45.5 MB each, which embed the style props.
  - `rowStart`/`colSpan`/... 9 MB, `placement` 17 MB, `direction` 12 MB.
- Source shapes:
  - styled-system/generated/system.gen.ts: 793 lines, 706 optional properties.
  - conditions.gen.ts: `Conditions` with 130 keys.
  - Each style property is `ConditionalValue<V>` (css.types.ts:32), which includes a `{ [K in keyof Conditions]?: ... }` object of 130 fields, each a depth-truncated text.
  - So one `SystemStyleObject` is about 706 × (literal union + 130 fields), and each of about 125 props holds its own copy.
- `--collapse-inherited-props none` (the weekly) does not change this. With the 256 KB prototype the weekly flags gave the same 108 MB output and 4.33 GB as the default. The weekly's extra cost on 0.11.0 (31.8 s, 42.7 GB) is the same blow-up.
- In the gate fixture (chakra-only, 787 components), the largest prop is 26 KB: there `@chakra-ui/react`'s style system is a dependency, so `SystemStyleObject` stays a name.

## 3. Why the arena guard did not bound it

- The bound exists only in `OnDemand`:
  - `DEFAULT_MAX_RSS_MIB = 768` (on_demand.rs:71).
  - It is checked in `warm` (on_demand.rs:491) and in `maintain` after each served request (on_demand.rs:643-652, gated by `Upkeep::checks_memory(self.served)`).
  - `stop_past_bound` (on_demand.rs:655-669) turns the checker off for the session.
  - `OnDemand` is used by the Storybook provider, the watch path and the binding, not by `extract`.
- `extract` takes `Pass::Extract` and uses `Teardown::OneShot` (extract.rs:181), then calls `resolve_cached_early`, `resolve_early` or `resolve` (extract.rs:187-190, lib.rs:159-208). None of them reads memory or carries a `max_rss_mib`.
- What the guard measures: `arena_mib()` runs `mincore` over `tsrs_core::reserve::base()..RESERVE` (checker.rs:164-171). That is the checker's nodes, symbols and types only. The converter's `PropType` trees, the memo (`State::memo`, convert.rs:495), `KeptProps`, `PartsSeen` and the merged `ParsedProp`s are all mimalloc heap, outside that range. A 768 MiB arena bound would read a few hundred MiB here while the process held 40 GB.
- When it checks: between requests. The 39 GB is built inside the first concurrent batch of 5 components (about 5 s), so a per-request check is too late even in `OnDemand`. A Storybook session opening one of those 5 components would build the same multi-GB tree before any check.
- The ADR 0026 memory gate measured `chakra-only` (dependency style system, 785 MiB) and the arena, so neither the fixture nor the metric could see a project-source style system.

## 4. Proposed bound

Part A: the size cut in the converter (keeps semantic answers, bounds output).
- Rule: in `Converter::convert` (convert.rs:674-700), after `uncached`, a converted type whose size passes a budget is replaced by `Truncated` with its name (`self.truncated`, convert.rs:953), and the memo stores the cut form. Measure the size as a node count kept alongside the memo entry, rather than serializing as the prototype does.
- Prototype (uncommitted, reverted in worktree agent-ae859a360675978f3): `serde_json::to_vec(&converted).len() > PROTO_MAX_BYTES` → `self.truncated(info, None, TruncationLimit::Depth)`.
  - 1,000,000 B budget: Chakra 6.47 GB footprint, 5.08 s, 178 MB output.
  - 256,000 B budget: Chakra 4.36 GB, 4.81 s, 108 MB output. With weekly flags: 4.33 GB, 4.73 s.
  - Mantine core (`packages/@mantine/core/src`; largest prop 196 KB): output identical with both budgets (stats excluded); 0.87 GB both ways.
  - Gate fixture `checker-default/chakra-only/src`: identical, about 0.70 GB.
- Rejected variant: capping project-declared objects below the top at 100 fields gets Chakra to 1.16 GB, 2.3 s and 10.7 MB, but changes Mantine's output (`classNames`, `styles`, `vars`, `getInputProps` in 24 of 348 components). It is not output-preserving.
- Budget choice: Mantine's largest whole prop is 196 KB, so 256 KB is close to it. 512 KB to 1 MB gives more margin at 4.4 to 6.5 GB. A node-count budget should be calibrated on the four weekly corpora before choosing.
- Needs a new `TruncationLimit` variant (for example `Size { nodes }`) or a documented reuse, plus a diagnostic. That is a schema and contract decision (ADR).

Part B: the hard heap budget on the one-shot path (guarantees a bound for any shape).
- Count converted nodes or bytes in a shared `AtomicU64` in `State`, incremented on each miss and each memo-hit clone (the size is known from the entry). Alternatively read mimalloc's committed bytes (`mi_process_info`), which also sees the clone.
- When the count passes `max_heap_mib` (default about 4 GiB, configurable, with the same knob reused by `OnDemand`), `convert` returns a new `CallError` variant. The component in flight, and every later one, keeps its structural answer. One `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` warning names the bound, as `stop_past_bound` does.
- Checked inside the conversion, not between requests, so the first batch cannot run away.
- Output under the bound is unchanged by construction. Gate fixture and Mantine are under 1 GB.

Part C (follow-up, not needed for the bound): stop deep-cloning on memo hits. Share converted subtrees (`Arc<PropType>` children, or a type table with references) so that a hit costs one pointer. This attacks the remaining ~40× ratio of memory to output (108 MB output → 4.36 GB). It touches the public core type and the serializers, so it is a larger change.

Also worth doing: `kept::save` should stream to the temporary file (`rmp_serde::encode::write` into a `BufWriter`) instead of building the whole buffer, which was 2.16 GB here.

Risks:
- The size cut changes output only for types over the budget. A project with legitimately large own types (a design-token object) loses their expansion, and a diagnostic must say so.
- Measuring size after `uncached` still builds the oversized tree once, transiently, per in-flight conversion (tens to hundreds of MB × up to 4 converters). Part B covers the worst case.
- The memo stores the cut form, so a type cut at one depth stays cut wherever it is recalled at that depth, as the existing caps already do.
- Part B makes results depend on a memory threshold. Past it, which components stay structural depends on order. The answer order is deterministic, but the result differs between machines if the default is derived from RAM, so keep it a constant.
- Serializing to measure (prototype) costs time: 1.0 → 1.35 s on Mantine. Use a node count.
- Add a gate fixture with a project-source style system (the Chakra corpus `src` itself, or a trimmed copy) to the ADR 0026 memory gate, measured as process footprint rather than arena residency.

1	//! Which inherited dependency sources are ambient: what every element has, or a style system, which a reader would not
2	//! lead with. The resolver collapses the large ones into a layer (names only) and lists every other dependency source,
3	//! which is the API a dependency's component exposes (its modes, state and composition).
4	//!
5	//! Which clause fits reads only the source's file, its type name and a prop's name; the resolver adds its size (below). It
6	//! is the rule measured in the "Layer-only props" section of `docs/measurement.md`; the test
7	//! `the_rule_gives_the_clause_the_oracles_classifier_gives` keeps this module equal to that classifier's recorded
8	//! verdicts. The first clause that fits decides:
9	//!
10	//! 1. **dom file**: the source's file is `@types/react`, or react-aria's `@react-types/shared/src/dom.d.ts`
11	//! 2. **dom type**: the source's type is a DOM family: `GlobalDOMEvents`, `DOMAttributes`, `AriaAttributes`,
12	//!    `AllHTMLAttributes`, `SVGAttributes`, `*HTMLAttributes`, `Aria*Attributes`
13	//! 3. **style type**: the source's type is a style system: `*StyleProps`, `*StyleProp`, `SystemProps`,
14	//!    `Space|Layout|Color|Typography|Border|Flex|Grid|Position|Shadow|Background` + `Props`
15	//! 4. **global attribute**: the prop is one every element has, or starts `aria-` or `data-`
16	//! 5. **dependency api**: anything else
17	//!
18	//! Clauses 1 to 3 decide a whole source: an ambient source is one the resolver may collapse, and only when it is also
19	//! large (`ResolutionContext::collapses`: a layer record costs more than a handful of props, and listing a small
20	//! ambient source gives `aria-label` and `id` their types). Clause 4 decides a prop of a source the first three did not
21	//! match; it never collapses a source on its own. A source that is API (clause 5) collapses only past
22	//! `LARGE_API_SOURCE` props, which no API measured on the pinned corpora and on apps reaches.
23	//!
24	//! Clause 4 is not part of the production rule: the resolver decides per source (`is_ambient_source`, clauses 1 to 3)
25	//! and never reads a prop's name. It is kept under `#[cfg(test)]` so the parity test can compare the whole classifier,
26	//! not only the source verdicts, with the oracle's.

33	    "style",
34	    "id",
35	    "title",
36	    "lang",
37	    "dir",
38	    "hidden",
39	    "tabIndex",
40	    "role",
41	    "slot",
42	    "accessKey",
43	    "draggable",
44	    "contentEditable",
45	    "spellCheck",
46	    "translate",
47	    "inputMode",
48	    "nonce",
49	];

51	/// Type names of the DOM families that are named exactly (the rest end in `HTMLAttributes` or are `Aria*Attributes`).
52	const DOM_TYPES: &[&str] =
53	    &["GlobalDOMEvents", "DOMAttributes", "AriaAttributes", "AllHTMLAttributes", "SVGAttributes"];
54	
55	/// The style-system prefixes that, with `Props`, name a style source (`SpaceProps`, `LayoutProps`, ...).
56	const STYLE_PREFIXES: &[&str] =
57	    &["Space", "Layout", "Color", "Typography", "Border", "Flex", "Grid", "Position", "Shadow", "Background"];
58	
59	/// Which clause of the rule decided. Only the parity test with the oracle's classifier reads the per-prop verdict; the
60	/// resolver needs the whole-source clauses (`is_ambient_source`).
61	#[cfg(test)]
62	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
63	enum Why {
64	    /// The source's file is a DOM declaration file (clause 1).
65	    DomFile,
66	    /// The source's type is a DOM family (clause 2).
67	    DomType,
68	    /// The source's type is a style system (clause 3).
69	    StyleType,
70	    /// The prop is one every element has (clause 4).
71	    GlobalAttribute,
72	    /// None of the above: a dependency's own API (clause 5).
73	    DependencyApi,
74	}
75	
76	#[cfg(test)]
77	impl Why {
78	    /// Whether the prop is ambient (clauses 1 to 4) and not API (clause 5).
79	    fn is_ambient(self) -> bool {
80	        self != Self::DependencyApi
81	    }
82	}
83	
84	/// `\w*` in the rule: letters, digits and underscore.
85	fn is_word(text: &str) -> bool {
86	    text.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_')
87	}
88	
89	fn is_dom_file(file: &str) -> bool {
90	    file.contains("/@types/react/")
91	        || file
92	            .rsplit_once("/@react-types/shared/src/")
93	            .is_some_and(|(_, name)| matches!(name, "dom.d.ts" | "dom.d.mts" | "dom.d.cts"))
94	}
95	
96	fn is_dom_type(type_name: &str) -> bool {
97	    DOM_TYPES.contains(&type_name)
98	        || type_name.strip_suffix("HTMLAttributes").is_some_and(is_word)
99	        || type_name.strip_prefix("Aria").and_then(|rest| rest.strip_suffix("Attributes")).is_some_and(is_word)
100	}
101	
102	fn is_style_type(type_name: &str) -> bool {
103	    type_name == "SystemProps"
104	        || type_name.strip_suffix("StyleProps").or_else(|| type_name.strip_suffix("StyleProp")).is_some_and(is_word)
105	        || STYLE_PREFIXES.iter().any(|prefix| type_name.strip_prefix(prefix) == Some("Props"))
106	}
107	
108	/// Whether `prop` is one every element has, or an `aria-` or `data-` attribute (clause 4).
109	#[cfg(test)]
110	fn is_global_attribute(prop: &str) -> bool {
111	    GLOBAL_ATTRIBUTES.contains(&prop) || prop.starts_with("aria-") || prop.starts_with("data-")
112	}
113	
114	/// Whether a source in `file` declaring the type `type_name` is ambient as a whole (clauses 1 to 3), so the resolver may
115	/// record it as a layer of names instead of listing its props (it does when the source is also large).
116	pub(crate) fn is_ambient_source(file: &str, type_name: &str) -> bool {
117	    is_dom_file(file) || is_dom_type(type_name) || is_style_type(type_name)
118	}
119	
120	/// The rule for one prop a collapsed source names: the clause that decided and so whether it is ambient or API.
121	#[cfg(test)]
122	fn classify(file: &str, type_name: &str, prop: &str) -> Why {
123	    if is_dom_file(file) {
124	        Why::DomFile
125	    } else if is_dom_type(type_name) {
126	        Why::DomType
127	    } else if is_style_type(type_name) {
128	        Why::StyleType
129	    } else if is_global_attribute(prop) {
130	        Why::GlobalAttribute
131	    } else {
132	        Why::DependencyApi
133	    }
134	}
135	
136	#[cfg(test)]
137	mod tests {
138	    use super::*;
139	    use rstest::rstest;
140	
141	    const REACT: &str = "/p/node_modules/@types/react/index.d.ts";
142	    const ARIA_DOM: &str = "/p/node_modules/@react-types/shared/src/dom.d.ts";
143	    const ARIA_DOM_MTS: &str = "/p/node_modules/@react-types/shared/src/dom.d.mts";
144	    const ARIA_EVENTS: &str = "/p/node_modules/@react-types/shared/src/events.d.ts";
145	    const PKG: &str = "/p/node_modules/x/index.d.ts";
146	
147	    #[rstest]
148	    #[case(REACT, "Anything", "foo", Why::DomFile)]
149	    #[case(ARIA_DOM, "GlobalDOMEvents", "onClick", Why::DomFile)]
150	    #[case(ARIA_DOM_MTS, "Other", "x", Why::DomFile)]
151	    #[case(ARIA_EVENTS, "KeyboardEvents", "onKeyDown", Why::DependencyApi)]
152	    #[case(PKG, "GlobalDOMEvents", "onClick", Why::DomType)]
153	    #[case(PKG, "DOMAttributes", "onClick", Why::DomType)]
154	    #[case(PKG, "AriaAttributes", "aria-label", Why::DomType)]
155	    #[case(PKG, "AllHTMLAttributes", "href", Why::DomType)]
156	    #[case(PKG, "SVGAttributes", "d", Why::DomType)]
157	    #[case(PKG, "HTMLAttributes", "dir", Why::DomType)]
158	    #[case(PKG, "ButtonHTMLAttributes", "type", Why::DomType)]
159	    #[case(PKG, "AriaLabelingAttributes", "aria-label", Why::DomType)]
160	    #[case(PKG, "AriaAttributesExtra", "foo", Why::DependencyApi)]
161	    #[case(PKG, "Aria_Attributes", "foo", Why::DomType)]
162	    #[case(PKG, "Aria-Attributes", "foo", Why::DependencyApi)]
163	    #[case(PKG, "StyleProps", "margin", Why::StyleType)]
164	    #[case(PKG, "JsxStyleProps", "margin", Why::StyleType)]
165	    #[case(PKG, "ViewStyleProp", "margin", Why::StyleType)]
166	    #[case(PKG, "SystemProps", "margin", Why::StyleType)]
167	    #[case(PKG, "SpaceProps", "m", Why::StyleType)]
168	    #[case(PKG, "BackgroundProps", "bg", Why::StyleType)]
169	    #[case(PKG, "Props", "m", Why::DependencyApi)]
170	    #[case(PKG, "ColorsProps", "m", Why::DependencyApi)]
171	    #[case(PKG, "StylePropsExtra", "m", Why::DependencyApi)]
172	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "className", Why::GlobalAttribute)]
173	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "aria-label", Why::GlobalAttribute)]
174	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "data-testid", Why::GlobalAttribute)]
175	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "tabIndex", Why::GlobalAttribute)]
176	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "value", Why::DependencyApi)]
177	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "defaultValue", Why::DependencyApi)]
178	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "type", Why::DependencyApi)]
179	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "name", Why::DependencyApi)]
180	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "disabled", Why::DependencyApi)]
181	    #[case(PKG, "DialogProps", "Aria-label", Why::DependencyApi)]
182	    fn the_clause_that_decides_is_the_first_that_fits(
183	        #[case] file: &str,
184	        #[case] type_name: &str,
185	        #[case] prop: &str,
186	        #[case] expected: Why,
187	    ) {
188	        assert_eq!(classify(file, type_name, prop), expected);
189	    }
190	
191	    /// `ambient_parity.json` holds the verdicts of the TypeScript classifier of the "Layer-only props" measurement
192	    /// (`docs/measurement.md`) for every distinct (file, type, prop) a collapsed layer names on antd and shadcn, plus
193	    /// synthetic edge cases (`/p/node_modules/x/index.d.ts`) for the style-system and DOM-type clauses, which those two
194	    /// corpora do not exercise (the verdicts are the classifier's, not written by hand). Chakra, Mantine and Spectrum
195	    /// are not in the data. This module must give the same clause for each.
196	    #[test]
197	    fn the_rule_gives_the_clause_the_oracles_classifier_gives() {
198	        let rows: Vec<serde_json::Value> = serde_json::from_str(include_str!("ambient_parity.json")).unwrap();
199	        assert!(rows.len() > 500, "{} rows", rows.len());
200	        let mut seen = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
201	        for row in &rows {
202	            let text = |key: &str| row[key].as_str().unwrap_or_else(|| panic!("{key} in {row}"));
203	            let (file, type_name, prop, label) = (text("file"), text("type"), text("prop"), text("why"));
204	            let expected = match label {
205	                "dom file" => Why::DomFile,
206	                "dom type" => Why::DomType,
207	                "style type" => Why::StyleType,
208	                "global attribute" => Why::GlobalAttribute,
209	                "dependency api" => Why::DependencyApi,
210	                other => panic!("unknown clause {other}"),
211	            };
212	            let got = classify(file, type_name, prop);
213	            assert_eq!(got, expected, "{file} {type_name} {prop}");
214	            assert_eq!(text("kind") == "ambient", got.is_ambient(), "{file} {type_name} {prop}");
215	            seen.insert(label.to_owned());
216	            // Clauses one to three decide a whole source, and so whether the resolver may collapse it.
217	            if matches!(expected, Why::DomFile | Why::DomType | Why::StyleType) {
218	                assert!(is_ambient_source(file, type_name), "{file} {type_name}");
219	            }
220	        }
221	        assert_eq!(seen.len(), 5, "every clause is covered: {seen:?}");
222	    }
223	
224	    #[test]
225	    fn only_clauses_one_to_three_collapse_a_source() {
226	        assert!(is_ambient_source(REACT, "X"));
227	        assert!(is_ambient_source(PKG, "GlobalDOMEvents"));
228	        assert!(is_ambient_source(PKG, "SystemProps"));
229	        // A source of global attributes only is not collapsed on its own: clause 4 decides a prop, not a source.
230	        assert!(!is_ambient_source(PKG, "DialogProps"));
231	    }
232	}

1	//! Options for one extraction run.
2	//!
3	//! These live in `types/` so the resolver and the dependency loader can read them without importing `pipeline`;
4	//! `pipeline` re-exports them, so `caliper_docgen_core::pipeline::PipelineOptions` and the others keep their paths.
5	
6	use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
7	use rustc_hash::FxHashSet;
8	use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
9	
10	/// How much of an inherited HTML element's attribute surface to expose.
11	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
12	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
13	pub enum HtmlAttributeMode {
14	    /// A compact subset per element: `ref`, `aria-*`, every event handler but the `*Capture` twins, the global
15	    /// attributes and the element's own notable ones, kept in `notableInherited`. Opt-in; `Full` is the default.
16	    Curated,
17	    /// Actually resolve `@types/react`'s real `HTMLAttributes`/`AriaAttributes`/
18	    /// `DOMAttributes`/`<Element>HTMLAttributes` interface chain, matching RDT's
19	    /// full ~250-300 attributes per element — the default.
20	    Full,
21	    /// Don't synthesize any inherited HTML attributes at all — own props only.
22	    None,
23	}
24	
25	impl HtmlAttributeMode {
26	    /// The mode named by a config or binding string. `Err` carries the unrecognized value, so callers can name it
27	    /// instead of silently falling back to a default.
28	    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, &str> {
29	        match s {
30	            "curated" => Ok(Self::Curated),
31	            "full" => Ok(Self::Full),
32	            "none" => Ok(Self::None),
33	            other => Err(other),
34	        }
35	    }
36	}
37	
38	/// Which inherited sources are recorded as an `InheritedLayer` of names instead of expanded prop by prop (collapse).
39	/// A component's own props type is always expanded. A dependency source collapses when it is ambient (DOM and ARIA
40	/// attributes, style systems) and declares more than 30 props; a dependency's own API is listed unless it declares more than 200 props.
41	#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
42	#[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")]
43	pub enum CollapseInheritedProps {
44	    /// Large ambient sources declared in a loaded dependency (`load_dependencies`).
45	    #[default]
46	    Dependencies,
47	    /// Those, and the project's own sources of more than 30 props.
48	    All,
49	    /// Expand every source.
50	    None,
51	}
52	
53	impl CollapseInheritedProps {
54	    /// The mode named by a config or binding string. `Err` carries the unrecognized value.
55	    pub fn parse(s: &str) -> Result<Self, &str> {
56	        match s {
57	            "dependencies" => Ok(Self::Dependencies),
58	            "all" => Ok(Self::All),
59	            "none" => Ok(Self::None),
60	            other => Err(other),
61	        }
62	    }
63	}
64	
65	/// Configuration for a single extraction run.
66	#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
67	pub struct PipelineOptions {
68	    /// Source directories to scan.
69	    pub src_dirs: Vec<Utf8PathBuf>,
70	    /// Extra gitignore-style glob patterns to exclude, relative to each source directory (on top of built-in: stories,
71	    /// tests, snapshots).
72	    pub exclude_patterns: Vec<String>,
73	    /// Component name prefixes to skip.
74	    pub exclude_prefixes: Vec<String>,
75	    /// How much of an inherited HTML element's attributes to expose.
76	    pub html_attributes: HtmlAttributeMode,
77	    /// Path to the tsconfig that governs module resolution. When unset, each importing file uses the nearest
78	    /// `tsconfig.json` above it, and the one above the first source directory supplies `customConditions`.
79	    pub tsconfig_path: Option<Utf8PathBuf>,
80	    /// Additional builtin type names beyond the React standard set.
81	    pub extra_builtins: FxHashSet<compact_str::CompactString>,
82	    /// Cache directory. Defaults to `node_modules/.cache/caliper-docgen` under the nearest ancestor of the first source
83	    /// directory that has a `node_modules` or a `package.json` (a directory in the OS temp directory when there is
84	    /// none), so the CLI, the Vite plugin and the Storybook addon share one cache whatever directory they run from.
85	    pub cache_dir: Option<Utf8PathBuf>,
86	    /// Read and write the on-disk caches (the declaration parse cache and the dependency index) under `cache_dir`.
87	    /// Off, a run reads and writes nothing there and parses everything; its output is the same. On by default.
88	    pub use_cache: bool,
89	    /// Load the dependency declarations project types reference, by name, before resolving (ADR 0010). On by default
90	    /// (`docs/performance.md`); off, a type imported from a package resolves only when it is a builtin or a known
91	    /// shortcut. A project with no installed packages loads nothing either way.
92	    pub load_dependencies: bool,
93	    /// Which large inherited sources to record as a layer instead of expanding.
94	    pub collapse_inherited_props: CollapseInheritedProps,
95	    /// Ask the built-in TypeScript checker for each component's props and merge them over the structural result
96	    /// (ADR 0026, `docs/type-checker-integration.md`). On by default; off, the structural resolver answers alone.
97	    /// `extract` ignores it: the checker backend lives in `caliper-docgen-semantic`, which depends on this crate, so
98	    /// the embedding (the CLI) runs it and calls [`crate::types::semantic::merge_semantic`].
99	    pub checker: bool,
100	}
101	
102	impl Default for PipelineOptions {
103	    fn default() -> Self {
104	        Self {
105	            src_dirs: vec![Utf8PathBuf::from("./src")],
106	            exclude_patterns: vec![],
107	            exclude_prefixes: vec![],
108	            html_attributes: HtmlAttributeMode::Full,
109	            tsconfig_path: None,
110	            extra_builtins: Default::default(),
111	            cache_dir: None,
112	            use_cache: true,
113	            load_dependencies: true,
114	            collapse_inherited_props: CollapseInheritedProps::default(),
115	            checker: true,
116	        }
117	    }
118	}
119	
120	impl PipelineOptions {
121	    /// Where the parse and dependency caches (and `extract`'s kept checker answer) live: `cache_dir` when set, else
122	    /// `node_modules/.cache/caliper-docgen` under the nearest ancestor of the first source directory that has a
123	    /// `node_modules` or a `package.json`, so running from another directory neither misses the project's cache nor
124	    /// creates a `node_modules` there. A source directory in no project gets a directory in the OS temp directory.
125	    pub fn effective_cache_dir(&self) -> Utf8PathBuf {
126	        if let Some(dir) = &self.cache_dir {
127	            return dir.clone();
128	        }
129	        const CACHE: &str = "node_modules/.cache/caliper-docgen";
130	        let root = canonicalize_first_src_dir(&self.src_dirs).and_then(|src| {
131	            src.ancestors()
132	                .find(|dir| dir.join("node_modules").is_dir() || dir.join("package.json").is_file())
133	                .map(Utf8Path::to_owned)
134	        });
135	        match root {
136	            Some(root) => root.join(CACHE),
137	            None => {
138	                let temp = std::env::temp_dir();
139	                Utf8PathBuf::from_path_buf(temp).unwrap_or_else(|_| Utf8PathBuf::from(".")).join("caliper-docgen-cache")
140	            }
141	        }
142	    }
143	}
144	
145	/// Canonicalize `src_dirs`' first entry to use as the "from" directory for
146	/// resolving @types/react and TypeScript's own lib.d.ts files — must match
147	/// what discovered file paths look like (always absolute — the `ignore`
148	/// walker absolutizes them regardless of whether --src was given as relative
149	/// or absolute), since the resolver looks this same specifier up again
150	/// per-component relative to each file's own absolute directory. A relative
151	/// src_dirs entry has too few path components for oxc_resolver's ancestor
152	/// walk to ever reach the real node_modules tree, so it silently finds
153	/// nothing instead of the intended real package.
154	pub(crate) fn canonicalize_first_src_dir(src_dirs: &[Utf8PathBuf]) -> Option<Utf8PathBuf> {
155	    src_dirs.first().and_then(|dir| crate::canonical_path::canonicalize(dir).ok())
156	}

def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props, and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    document = schema_version.check(json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]), 'weekly')
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])
        members[(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName']))] = names
    return members

def caliper_layer_members(binary, src, root):
    """The props Caliper's collapsed inheritance layers hold, as (file, name) -> prop names: the output names them in a
    layer instead of listing them as props, and the canonical JSON is the one that carries the layers."""
    command = [binary, 'extract', '--src', src, '--json', '--html-attributes', 'full', '--include-unexported', '--quiet',
               '--load-dependencies', '--collapse-inherited-props', 'none']
    out = subprocess.run(command, capture_output=True, text=True, check=True).stdout
    document = schema_version.check(json.loads(out[out.index('{'):]), 'weekly')
    lists = document.get('nameLists', {})
    members = {}
    for c in document['components'].values():
        names = set()
        for layer in c.get('inheritance', []):
            if layer.get('members'):
                names |= set(lists[layer['members']])
        members[(relative(c['filePath'], root), norm_name(c['displayName']))] = names
    return members

content.content:
By default (`collapseInheritedProps: dependencies`) Caliper collapses a large ambient inherited dependency source (DOM and ARIA attributes, style systems; more than 30 props) into a layer (ADR 0012; `docs/architecture/resolver-type-resolution.md`, Collapse) and lists only its notable members as props. A dependency's own API is listed in full (a source past 200 props that is not ambient by name still collapses). The Storybook addon runs with `collapseInheritedProps: none`, which lists every inherited prop; the layers below are what the CLI, the NAPI binding and agents reading the output see. A prop in a layer is in the output, named by the layer's `members`, but is not in the flat list, so the table reports both: the plain columns say what the default output lists, "with layers" says what it holds. react-docgen writes no layers, so its two columns are equal.

RDT has mistakes of its own. With `--oracle` the run also asks TypeScript 7.1's checker (`apps/oracle/src/oracle.ts`, `typescript-beta/sync`, the `7.1.0-beta` package) for each prop's type and compares it structurally with Caliper's canonical `--json`, extracted with `--html-attributes full --include-unexported --load-dependencies --collapse-inherited-props none`. The weekly table shows the share of props that agree (identical, or the same type spelled by name) and the share the checker contradicts, for Caliper, RDT and react-docgen, and the headline below. `agree` is the loose number; `wrong` is the one that matters and the one the weekly issue gates on, but the comparator has artifacts that make it both over- and under-report. `docs/rdt-differences.md` lists every class of disagreement with an example, how it is counted and whether the comparator scored it right. The checker is a beta, so a disagreement is a reason to look, not a verdict on its own. The weekly extracts with the default, the checker, so from `oracle.universe_version` 5 this compares the checker's own answer, merged over the structural one, with the checker's: it agrees almost by construction, and a `wrong` there is a prop the merge changed or kept structural against the checker (`docs/type-checker-integration.md`). The structural resolver alone was judged until version 4.

### Layer-only props

**Which configuration this describes.** The CLI, the NAPI binding and the Vite plugin collapse by default (`collapseInheritedProps: 'dependencies'`). Large inherited sources are collapsed by default, wherever they are declared, and the checker's answer is collapsed the same way.

Breaking for the Storybook addon: its default output changes. `collapseInheritedProps` now defaults to `'dependencies'` instead of `'none'`, so an inherited source too large to be an API (a dependency's DOM, ARIA or style-system set of more than 30 props, or any source of more than 200 props) is one inheritance layer of names instead of hundreds of Controls rows. A component's own props and the notable inherited ones are still listed. Set `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` to list every inherited prop as before.

For every consumer, the default `dependencies` mode now also collapses a source in the project's own code that declares more than 200 props (a design system's style props, such as Chakra's `SystemProperties` in Chakra's own repository); before, only dependency sources collapsed. With the checker on, the props a collapsed layer names are no longer also listed from the checker's answer, and a large dependency source only the checker could reach (react-aria's `GlobalDOMEvents` handlers) becomes a layer by the same rule.

The default collapseInheritedProps mode (dependencies) now also collapses a
project source declaring more than 200 props (LARGE_API_SOURCE), by its size
alone: a style system in the project's own source (Chakra's SystemProperties,
705 props) collapses as an installed one does. The rule moves to
CollapseInheritedProps::collapses so both lanes use it.

The checker's merge lays its props out in the same layers: a prop a collapsed
structural layer names is left to the layer, and a source only the checker
reached (react-aria's GlobalDOMEvents handlers) becomes a layer when the rule
collapses it, counted over the props of the answer.

The Storybook addon defaults to 'dependencies' instead of 'none' (breaking:
its default output changes; 'none' still lists everything), and the weekly
follows the addon's configuration.

1	// `__docgenInfo` (react-docgen-typescript's shape) to argTypes, the way `@storybook/react`'s own docgen worker does it
2	// (src/docgen/buildDocgen.ts): React's `Attributes`, `RefAttributes` and `ClassAttributes` props from node_modules are
3	// dropped, defaults are marked `computed: false`, and React's `extractArgTypes` converts the rest. Calling React's
4	// converter, not a copy of it, keeps controls, type summaries and default-value summaries identical to Storybook's.
5	
6	import type { RdtComponentDoc, RdtProp } from 'caliper-docgen-napi'
7	import type { StrictArgTypes } from 'storybook/internal/types'
8	
9	/** `parameters.docs.extractArgTypes` from `@storybook/react/entry-preview-argtypes`. */
10	export type ExtractArgTypes = (component: { __docgenInfo: RdtComponentDoc }) => StrictArgTypes | null
11	
12	const REACT_ATTRIBUTE_INTERFACES = new Set(['Attributes', 'RefAttributes', 'ClassAttributes'])
13	
14	function isReactAttribute(prop: RdtProp): boolean {
15	  return (
16	    prop.parent !== null &&
17	    REACT_ATTRIBUTE_INTERFACES.has(prop.parent.name) &&
18	    /(^|[\\/])node_modules[\\/]/.test(prop.parent.fileName)
19	  )
20	}
21	
22	export function toArgTypes(doc: RdtComponentDoc, extractArgTypes: ExtractArgTypes): StrictArgTypes | undefined {
23	  const props = Object.fromEntries(
24	    Object.entries(doc.props)
25	      .filter(([, prop]) => !isReactAttribute(prop))
26	      .map(([name, prop]) => [
27	        name,
28	        prop.defaultValue ? { ...prop, defaultValue: { ...prop.defaultValue, computed: false } } : prop,
29	      ]),
30	  )
31	  return extractArgTypes({ __docgenInfo: { ...doc, props } }) ?? undefined
32	}
33	
34	/** React's converter, loaded on first use: it is a preview entry, so only a docgen request should pay for it. */
35	export async function loadExtractArgTypes(): Promise<ExtractArgTypes> {
36	  const { parameters } = (await import('@storybook/react/entry-preview-argtypes')) as {
37	    parameters: { docs: { extractArgTypes: ExtractArgTypes } }
38	  }
39	  return parameters.docs.extractArgTypes
40	}
